title: Accenture, Google Cloud Launch Unit Deploying 1,000 AI Engineers On-Site
excerpt: Google Cloud will train up to 1,000 Accenture engineers to work inside client offices building AI applications — the industry's latest bet that embedded, forward-deployed talent is the key to AI returns.
body:
• Accenture and Google Cloud have formed the Accenture Gemini Enterprise Business Group, a new unit aimed at deploying Google's agentic AI platform inside client companies.
  • Google Cloud will train up to 1,000 Accenture "forward-deployed engineers" to work on-site with customers, planning and building AI applications on the Gemini Enterprise platform.
  • The move bets that embedding engineers inside client offices — a model popularized by Palantir — is the key to turning enterprise AI experiments into returns.
  • The group builds on Accenture's nearly 50,000 Google Cloud-skilled professionals and follows a Gemini Enterprise Acceleration Program the two companies began in April.

Accenture and Google Cloud have launched a new unit to put AI engineers directly inside their clients' offices, betting that hands-on, on-site work is the missing ingredient in enterprise AI adoption. The Accenture Gemini Enterprise Business Group, first reported by the Wall Street Journal on September 8, will deploy Accenture consultants trained by Google Cloud to build agentic AI applications on the Gemini Enterprise platform.

Under the arrangement, Google Cloud will train up to 1,000 Accenture forward-deployed engineers — or FDEs — who will work with clients on-site to plan and build AI applications. The group will also draw on other Accenture experts and a small group of Google Cloud engineers for limited engagements with top-tier customers, according to the WSJ.

Why engineers in the room matter

The FDE model was popularized by Palantir, which built its business by embedding technologists inside customer organizations. AI companies are now copying it aggressively. Google Cloud earlier this year launched a $750 million partner ecosystem commitment embedding its FDEs across consultancies including Capgemini, Cognizant and Deloitte, plus a multi-year partnership with CVC Capital Partners to deploy FDEs into its portfolio companies. Rivals are moving the same way: OpenAI has set up "The Deployment Co.," while firms like Ode embed engineers with Anthropic.

"Clients want clear value and they're stuck. We promised AI can do that. And they're like, 'We get it, except it's not happening, help us make it happen.'"

— Julie Sweet, Chair and CEO, Accenture

The urgency reflects the industry's core problem: nearly four years after ChatGPT's debut, the return on enterprise AI spending remains hit-or-miss. According to August Ramp data cited by TechCrunch, Google accounts for roughly 6% of enterprise AI spending among Ramp's U.S. customers, versus 43.5% for Anthropic and 39.7% for OpenAI — a Google spokesperson noted the data excludes large strategic enterprise deals beyond model API usage. Companies struggle to integrate AI tools into corporate systems and customize them for specific business needs, and many lack the data pipelines and internal expertise to do it alone.

"There's a need for experts who can go and do these [things] for customers," Google Cloud chief executive Thomas Kurian told the Journal.

What the new group will do

According to Accenture's announcement, the business group will operate across the full Gemini Enterprise portfolio with four priorities: increasing adoption of Gemini Enterprise through proprietary accelerators and implementation frameworks; building repeatable, industry-specific solutions that reduce time-to-value; bridging the gap between AI experimentation and enterprise-scale transformation with dedicated capability centers; and expanding training and certification.

The partnership builds on five months of joint work. Google Cloud and Accenture started the Gemini Enterprise Acceleration Program in April, pairing engineers from both companies on customer projects and providing access to Google DeepMind models.

"The companies seeing the greatest outcomes from AI are unlocking new growth, increasing productivity and resilience, and creating better experiences for their customers and employees."

— Julie Sweet, Chair and CEO, Accenture

It also adds to Accenture's own wave of FDE programs this year, which include a Microsoft FDE practice launched in March, an FDE initiative with ServiceNow in May, and a joint program with SAP in June, according to TechCrunch.

The diaspora connection

Accenture employs tens of thousands of technology professionals of Indian origin across India and the United States, and Indian global capability centers are deeply involved in enterprise AI rollouts for multinational clients. A 1,000-strong FDE workforce is also a talent signal: the model rewards engineers who combine business judgment with agentic AI skills, exactly the profile India's large services workforce is racing to build. Notably, as eWeek reported, Gemini Enterprise does not lock every task to a Google model — it supports more than 200 models including Anthropic's Claude and Meta's Llama — so the engineers being trained will work across a multi-model landscape.

What to watch

The question is whether on-site engineers can move the needle on measurable outcomes where product features alone have not. Accenture says the group will focus on helping clients achieve outcomes from agentic AI "faster," with industry-specific solutions and implementation frameworks. Watch for named customer deployments and disclosed ROI figures over the coming quarters — those, more than headcount announcements, will show whether the forward-deployed model delivers.
